verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's own product page says the RTX PRO 6000 is optimized for CUDA-X libraries such as RAPIDS and accelerates AI work across TensorFlow and PyTorch. Community builders report running inference workloads on it under CUDA. However, none of the CUDA Toolkit evidence explicitly lists this part or its SM120 compute capability as a supported target, and one community critic says SM120 lacks support in the main libraries, which target SM100. missing for 10: an explicit CUDA Toolkit supported-GPU/compute-capability listing naming the RTX PRO 6000, documentation of library coverage for SM120 features, independent confirmation of toolchain maturity.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship GPU-compute workloads on the vendor's toolchain — CUDA or ROCm/HIP documentation lists this part as a supported target

citations.quote: Optimized for NVIDIA CUDA-X™ libraries like RAPIDS, it supercharges GPU-accelerated analytics and AI tasks
